items.title: CVE-2026-81673 (CRITICAL 9.3): The ‘/ws/apitribuna/setVisita’ endpoint is vulnerable to SQL injection through the id_video and id_ambito par…
items.one_liner: A critical SQL injection in the setVisita endpoint highlights input handling flaws that attackers can leverage to manipulate database records.
items.summary: A critical SQL injection vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-81673 has been identified in the ‘/ws/apitribuna/setVisita’ endpoint. The flaw stems from a failure to validate or sanitize the id_video and id_ambito parameters before inserting them into SQL queries. This allows remote attackers to disrupt query execution, trigger database errors, and manipulate visit tracking records. The vulnerability carries a CVSS base score of 9.3 and was published on August 27, 2026. Ultimately, it affects the overall integrity of analytics and record accuracy.
items.bottom_line: Unvalidated parameters in the setVisita endpoint allow remote SQL injection, threatening database integrity and visit tracking accuracy.

items.title: jvmi7/OfflinePainter — Offline Ed25519 signing toolkit - sign files, verify signatures, exchange keys via QR. Pure-Python RFC 8032, s
items.one_liner: An air-gapped, pure-Python Ed25519 signing and QR exchange toolkit provides dependency-free cryptographic operations for isolated machines.
items.summary: OfflinePainter is a pure-Python Ed25519 signing toolkit designed for air-gapped environments that handles file signing, signature verification, and QR-based key exchange without third-party dependencies. It uses standard library modules like hashlib, hmac, base64, os, and zlib, implementing an RFC 8032 Ed25519 core from scratch. Secret keys can be optionally encrypted using scrypt passphrases, and key material or signatures can be transferred across air gaps using SGDK1 QR payloads. Additionally, the package includes a minimal Android demo app to facilitate scanning QR keys and performing sign or verify operations.
key_facts: Dependencies: Zero third-party Python stdlib only
items.bottom_line: Developers needing air-gapped cryptographic signing can utilize a zero-dependency Python implementation that avoids clipboard exposure by transferring keys via QR codes.

items.title: CamoDocs: A Poisoning Attack Against Retrieval-Augmented Language Models Using Camouflaged Documents
items.one_liner: CamoDocs is a RAG data poisoning attack that uses token dispersion and camouflaged document chunking to bypass query-overlap detection.
items.summary: Data poisoning attacks against Retrieval-Augmented Generation models typically rely on query inclusion, which introduces lexical and embedding-space artifacts that simple security defenses easily detect. Researchers introduce CamoDocs, a poisoning method that bypasses query inclusion by chunking synthesized benign and adversarial drafts, replacing selected tokens in benign chunks with dispersion tokens, and applying coherence filtering. Across seven RAG defenses, three open-weight LLMs, and three benchmarks, CamoDocs achieves high attack success rates while avoiding traditional detection artifacts. It also proves effective against proprietary systems, achieving average attack success rates of 61.80% on GPT-5.4-mini and 55.09% on Claude-Haiku-4.5. While erasure-heavy clustering defenses like TrustRAG mitigate the attack, they impose substantial utility drops on retrieval-dependent tasks.
items.bottom_line: RAG systems remain vulnerable to stealthy data poisoning techniques that evade lexical detection filters without sacrificing attack success rates.

claims.text: We propose CamoDocs, a poisoning attack that avoids direct query inclusion by camouflaging adversarial documents among benign content.
claims.support_span: We proposes CamoDocs, a poisoning attack that avoids direct query inclusion by camouflaging adversarial documents among benign content.

items.title: Safety Does Not Compose: Non-Decaying Loop State for Autonomous LLM Agents
items.one_liner: LoopHarness provides a persistent, non-decaying safety state across LLM agent loops to prevent multi-iteration fragmented attacks.
items.summary: Autonomous LLM agents operate in unattended loops across many iterations, but standard safeguards are defined over a single trajectory and re-initialized when a new trajectory begins. The authors show a theoretical separation: trajectory-scoped monitors fail against attacks whose evidence is fragmented across iterations, whereas a monitor retaining cross-iteration state succeeds. While geometrically decaying risk scores are insufficient due to fixed wait times, the authors introduce LoopHarness, which enforces a persistent, non-decaying safety state at the loop level. Under mediated commits and an arbiter detection floor, LoopHarness bounds unauthorized irreversible actions to a constant term, surviving fully colluding verifiers.
items.bottom_line: Trajectory-scoped monitors fail against multi-step attacks, requiring loop-level persistent state architectures to bound unauthorized actions.

claims.text: Our central result is a separation: against an attack whose evidence is fragmented across several iterations, every trajectory-scoped monitor has a true-positive rate equal to its false-positive rate...
claims.support_span: Our central result is a separation: against an attack whose evidence is fragmented across several iterations, every trajectory-scoped monitor has a true-positive rate equal to its false-positive rate, however expressive it is, because the evidence it would need never appears in the window it sees...

items.title: ROPE: Routed Origin Policy Enforcement against Indirect Prompt Injection
items.one_liner: ROPE uses structural origin tracking to block indirect prompt injections in tool-using LLM agents while preserving utility.
items.summary: Routed Origin Policy Enforcement (ROPE) is a novel defense mechanism designed to prevent indirect prompt injection in tool-using LLM agents. ROPE enforces a structural notion of trust where values can only reach state-changing tools if they trace unforgeably to explicit user requests, named sources, or authoritative records. By performing a deterministic origin check over sensitive tool parameters without relying on language models for the enforcement step, ROPE limits attack success rates to 1.6–2.6% while retaining up to 100% of clean utility. The framework maintains zero success rates against long-horizon attacks that defeat conventional system-level defenses.
items.bottom_line: ROPE stops indirect prompt injections in LLM agents by enforcing deterministic origin checks on sensitive tool parameters.

claims.text: ROPE holds attack success rate to 1.6--2.6% while retaining 82--100% of undefended clean utility, significantly exceeding state-of-the-art system-level defenses in utility while attaining comparable or better security.

items.title: Threat Actors Abuse Cursor Agent AI to Assist Ransomware Operations
items.one_liner: Aurora ransomware actors abused SpaceX's Cursor Agent with Claude Sonnet to automate reconnaissance and post-compromise tasks.
items.summary: Aurora ransomware operators have integrated SpaceX's AI Cursor Agent running Claude Sonnet into their post-compromise attack chain across multiple victims. Threat actors leveraged the AI tool to automate environment reconnaissance, execute Nmap and NetExec scans, configure VPN clients, and launch NTLM relay and certificate attacks using tools like PetitPotam and Certipy. Additionally, the group deployed a new Linux ransomware variant specifically tailored to target VMware ESXi hypervisors by scanning networks with custom LDAP modules.
items.bottom_line: Expect threat actors to actively weaponize AI developer coding agents for automated lateral movement and environment enumeration during intrusions.
